title: The Rise and Fall of the Five-Day Week

paragraphs.en: The five-day working week is a relatively recent invention. It became the standard in industrialised countries only after unions fought for it in the early twentieth century.
paragraphs.zh: 每周五天工作制是一个相对较新的发明。直到二十世纪初工会为之斗争之后，它才成为工业化国家的标准。

paragraphs.en: Now the arrangement is being questioned again. A growing number of trials suggest that a four-day week can maintain productivity while improving workers' wellbeing.
paragraphs.zh: 如今这一安排再次受到质疑。越来越多的试验表明，每周四天工作制在保持生产率的同时，还能改善员工的福祉。

paragraphs.en: In one large experiment, employees reported lower stress and burnout, and few firms observed a drop in output. Some even reported higher revenues.
paragraphs.zh: 在一项大型实验中，员工报告压力和倦怠感降低，几乎没有公司观察到产出下降。有些公司甚至报告收入增加。

paragraphs.en: Critics caution that the results may not apply everywhere. Service industries that must cover evenings and weekends cannot simply close their doors on Fridays.
paragraphs.zh: 批评者警告说，这些结果可能并非放之四海而皆准。必须覆盖晚间和周末的服务行业不能简单地在周五关门。

paragraphs.en: Still, the debate marks a shift in thinking about time. If technology makes us more productive per hour, perhaps we should work fewer hours rather than produce more.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管如此，这场争论标志着关于时间的观念转变。如果技术让我们每小时更有效率，也许我们应该减少工作时间，而不是生产更多。

paragraphs.en: The future of work, it seems, is not merely about where we work, but about how we value the time we have.
paragraphs.zh: 看来，工作的未来不仅关乎我们在哪里工作，更关乎我们如何珍视所拥有的时间。
